clue.text: Fit retaining 45-inch screw

indicators.note: something retaining another thing holds it within, so one word keeps the other inside it

parts.note: fit in the sense of suitable or appropriate means proper
an ell is an old cloth measure of 45 inches

explanation.surface: Some fitting holds a screw of a particular 45-inch size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fit' looks like a verb, but it is the adjective proper, opened up to hold ELL.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's screw is the rotating bladed device that drives it, the same thing as a propeller.

clue.text: Man on board with gun

definitions.meaning: a chessman or draughtsman moved about a board

explanation.definitionFit: Both a chessman and a handgun are informally called by this one word.

clue.text: Boring part in exam that's revolutionary

indicators.note: one word sits in the middle of the other, so the exam word encloses the drilling piece

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination
the bit is the part of a drill that does the boring

explanation.surface: A dull section of an examination turns out to be revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' suggests tedious, but it means drilling.
explanation.definitionFit: Orbital describes movement in an orbit, revolving around a body, which is revolutionary in the literal sense.

clue.text: Eastern lake found in the West? Strange

parts.note: Lake Erie is one of the Great Lakes, in the western hemisphere

explanation.surface: An eastern lake turning up in the West would indeed be strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie means weird and unsettling, a near synonym of strange.

clue.text: Caught girl with nothing on with boy

parts.note: lass is a word for a girl, especially in the north of Britain
O, the shape of zero, stands for nothing
Ed is a short boy's name

explanation.surface: A girl wearing nothing was caught with a boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with nothing on' paints an unclothed girl; it just puts O after LASS.
explanation.definitionFit: To be lassoed is to be caught with a rope noose, so caught is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Starting to steal at home, thug was outlawed

definitions.text: Starting to steal at home, thug was outlawed

parts.note: to rob is to steal
in means at home, as in staying in
a hood, short for hoodlum, is a thug

explanation.surface: A thug who started stealing at home became an outlaw.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the legendary outlaw of Sherwood Forest, who stole from the rich.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary English outlaw famed for robbing the rich is described by the whole clue.

clue.text: Grouse meat

definitions.meaning: to grouse is to complain, a sense shared by ... as a verb or noun

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a grumble or complaint and the meat of cattle.

clue.text: Base and vicious, determined to torment

parts.note: a bed is a base or foundation, as in a bed of concrete
evil means wicked or vicious

explanation.surface: Someone base and vicious sets out to torment others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Base' reads as an adjective like 'vicious', but it is the noun bed; 'and' and 'determined to' only join.
explanation.definitionFit: To bedevil is to plague or harass, much the same as torment.

clue.text: Tim agreed to move, went overseas

indicators.note: letters made to move are shifted about into a new order

explanation.surface: Tim agreed to relocate, and duly went abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to move' looks like part of what Tim agreed to, but it scrambles TIMAGREED.
explanation.definitionFit: To emigrate is to leave one's country to live in another, typically overseas.

clue.text: The underworld's guard dog of choice?

definitions.text: The underworld's guard dog of choice?

parts.words: The underworld's guard dog of choice?
parts.note: the mythical three-headed hound guarding Hades; 'of choice' teases a preferred breed of guard dog

explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the three-headed dog guarding the gates of Hades bears this name.

clue.text: Flat for those not wishing to move when they retire

definitions.text: Flat for those not wishing to move when they retire

parts.words: Flat for those not wishing to move when they retire
parts.note: a one-room flat where bed and sitting room are one, so retiring to bed needs no move

explanation.definitionFit: A one-room rented flat combining bedroom and sitting room, so going to bed needs no walk.

clue.text: Pay to stay

definitions.meaning: to pay off what is owed, as in clearing a bill
to make one's home somewhere, as in putting down roots

explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both paying an account and staying put in a new home.

clue.text: His appetite is all-consuming

parts.note: a creature that eats both plants and animals literally consumes all kinds of food

explanation.definitionFit: An animal eating both plant and animal food has an appetite that takes in everything.

clue.text: Way a convict joined a WWII prison

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
a lag, or old lag, is British slang for a convict

explanation.surface: A convict was taken along a road to a Second World War prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalag was a German camp for prisoners of war during the Second World War.

clue.text: Skinny, toothless what's-his-name

parts.note: skinny means thin
a toothless mouth shows only gums, so it is gummy

explanation.surface: Describing a thin man with no teeth whose name escapes you.
explanation.definitionFit: A placeholder word used for a person or thing whose name one cannot recall.

clue.text: Shining example of brat eager to reform

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so these letters are reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: A model pupil of a brat who is keen to mend his ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shining example' sounds like a role model; it is a constellation of bright stars. BRATEAGER is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The constellation also called the Plough is a shining group of stars, a literal shining example.

clue.text: Doctor needs work permits to provide drips

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
to let is to permit

explanation.surface: A doctor needs work permits before he can supply drips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drips' suggests hospital intravenous drips, but it means small drops of liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: Droplets are tiny drops of liquid, which is what drips are.

clue.text: Not always the products of great minds!

definitions.text: Not always the products of great minds!

parts.words: Not always the products of great minds!
parts.note: ambitious grand schemes may come from anyone, wise or foolish, so are not only produced by brilliant thinkers

explanation.definitionFit: Grand ambitious plans or concepts, which sound clever but are often dreamt up by anyone.

clue.text: Plainly distressed, but retains composure

indicators.note: read as com-posure, being composed or put together afresh, it signals the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone visibly upset nonetheless keeps their composure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composure' seems to mean calm, but it rearranges RETAINS; 'but' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone weeping openly is visibly upset, the plain sign of distress.

clue.text: Bungle a pay rise?

definitions.meaning: to make a mess of something
screw is old slang for wages, so an increase in it is the screw going upward

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a blunder, and whimsically also an increase in one's screw, slang for wages.

clue.text: Fears the end of combined studies

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word that follows is taken

parts.note: to read a subject at university is to study it

explanation.surface: Someone fears the final stretch of a joint degree course.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'read' a subject is the British way of saying to study it at university.
explanation.definitionFit: To dread something is to fear it greatly, so dreads is a synonym for fears.

clue.text: Grenade thrown — go on the defensive

indicators.note: letters thrown about land in a new order

explanation.surface: A grenade is hurled, so it is time to take cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown' fits a grenade naturally but it scrambles GRENADE.
explanation.definitionFit: The fencer's call warning an opponent to adopt a guarding stance, so a call to go on the defensive.

clue.text: A good mixer, maybe, but a troublemaker

definitions.meaning: a device that stirs or shakes liquids, such as in a washing machine

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a stirring device and a person who incites political trouble.

clue.text: One side getting nothing in agreement

parts.note: right is one side, as opposed to left
O, the shape of zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: One faction gains nothing from the deal they agreed.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a noun for a word of assent; 'getting' and 'in' only join.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal British exclamation of assent, used to signal agreement.

clue.text: Knave withdrawn from the pack?

definitions.meaning: a knave is a dishonest scoundrel
an animal living apart from its herd or pack is called a solitary beast of this kind

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a rascal, and also a lone animal that has split from its herd.

clue.text: It may be held up or down

indicators.note: in a down entry the word reads the same upwards or downwards, being a palindrome

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Something that can be raised or lowered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held up or down' suggests lifting; a belief is held, and the word reads the same both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A principle or belief is something a person holds, so it may be held.

clue.text: Puncture politician caught in a lie, perhaps

indicators.note: one piece is caught inside another, enclosed by it
perhaps suggests the letters may be arranged differently

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Puncturing a politician who has been caught out in a lie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges A LIE into IALE, and 'caught in' puts MP inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To impale is to pierce through with a sharp point, a form of puncturing.

clue.text: Betting, using a payphone

parts.note: pay gives wage, money earned
phone gives ring, to call someone up

explanation.surface: Placing bets by calling from a public telephone.
explanation.walkthrough: The single word 'payphone' must be read as two words, pay and phone; 'using a' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagering is placing a bet, so it means the same as betting.

clue.text: Witnesses a key agreement

parts.note: E is one of the musical keys
yes is a word of agreement

explanation.surface: Witnesses reach a key agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye something is to watch it, so eyes as a verb means witnesses or sees.

clue.text: Speak for traveller with grudge

parts.note: a rep, or commercial traveller, is a travelling salesperson
to resent is to grudge

explanation.surface: Speaking on behalf of a travelling salesman who holds a grudge.
explanation.walkthrough: A commercial traveller is an old British term for a sales rep.
explanation.definitionFit: To represent someone is to act or speak on their behalf.
